background.title: Reserve Bank of India
background.extract: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is the central bank of the Republic of India. It was established on 1 April 1935 by the British Raj, with enactment of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934. Although, the RBI is owned by the Government of India, the RBI is an autonomous regulatory organisation for the Indian banking and financial system, exercising substantial amount of independence and power over the Indian economy. It is responsible for the issue, supply and control of the Indian rupee. It also manages the country's main payment systems and the foreign exchange under the FEMA Act, 1999.
